items.note: Every shard runs vitest with --maxWorkers=2, set in unit-tests.yml only, as the IMPL says. Running two workers exposed a hidden harness bug. Fully synchronous test files never let the worker read RPC replies, so a file running past vitest's 60s RPC timeout fails the run with 'Timeout calling onTaskUpdate' even though every test passed. scenes-timeline.test.tsx took 66-79s on CI and hit it. I reproduced it locally with a 65s synchronous file: exit 1, then exit 0 after the fix. The fix is an afterEach in src/test-setup.ts that yields one setImmediate turn, using a reference taken before any test can install fake timers. All 45 fake-timer test files pass with it.

4-shard matrix (fail-fast false, timeout 12) with blob and dot reporters, thresholds zeroed on shards, blobs uploaded (include-hidden-files, retention 1). The final job keeps the id and name 'vitest', runs with if: !cancelled(), timeout 12, and its first step exits 1 unless needs.vitest-shard.result == success. It then runs vitest --merge-reports --coverage, which enforces the 60% thresholds. I changed one part of the IMPL. In vitest 3.2.7, --merge-reports only merges the coverage the blobs carry and never adds untested files (coverage provider mergeReports in node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.DfSpMS-b.js). With coverage.all=false on every shard, the denominator would shrink to loaded files only (shown locally: merged 1972/6430 instead of the full set). So shard 1 keeps coverage.all on (COVERAGE_ALL: matrix.shard == 1) and shards 2-4 turn it off. A local equivalence check gave identical totals for one unsharded run and the merged 4 shards: 334 files, 1744/34570. On CI the merged result is 92016/139323 (66.04%), against 91696/139024 (65.95%) on main. The extra 299 statements are the new source files.

Removed the src/app/**/*.test.ts jsdom mapping. mock-fetch-gate.test.ts already had a jsdom docblock. All 194 src/app .test.ts files pass under node (1723 tests), and their environment time fell to 0.45s. No other file needed a docblock.

src/test-setup.ts imports @testing-library/react dynamically, only when document exists. Docblock-jsdom files still get cleanup (14-file DOM sample and the remotion and mdx tests pass). Setup time summed over all files fell from 101s on main to 32.4s on CI.

scripts/ci/vitest-timing-summary.mjs reads blob directories or files (with its own small flatted decoder) and the JSON reporter format. It writes per-shard totals, the phase sums and the slowest N files to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, prints ::warning:: for files over 10s and for tests+setup+environment over 850s, writes a compact vitest-timings.json and always exits 0. The merge job runs it on the downloaded blobs, so no extra test run is needed. On CI it flagged scenes-timeline (79s), regex-bounds (34s), compositions-timeline (12s) and ReportProblemModal (10.7s). 8 vitest tests cover it, including the never-fail path.

The six retry-path tests use vi.useFakeTimers({toFake:['setTimeout']}), advance 3000ms and restore real timers in afterEach. The file went from 18s to 7ms. With a 1000ms advance the tests time out, so the backoff path really runs.
Only removed the duplicate certTier line in scripts/register-greet-anton-standalone.ts. coverage.all stays at its global default.

Replaced npx wait-on with a bounded 60x curl --max-time 5 loop that exits 1 with an ::error if the server never answers (checked locally against a closed port). Added actions/cache for .next/cache, keyed on the lockfile plus src/next.config.ts/mdx-components.tsx hashes, with a restore-key. I skipped the Playwright browser cache: the verifier measured about 10s of gain because --with-deps still runs apt. The repo's global pre-commit secret scan blocks any commit of 0826-e2e.yml because the file already had a placeholder Postgres URI with inline credentials in it. Instead of --no-verify, the disposable service now uses POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust and a password-free DATABASE_URL (separate commit). I also widened the E2E paths with next.config.ts, mdx-components.tsx, tsconfig.json and .npmrc. A dispatched E2E run on the branch passed (38936820151).

pull_request now has a paths filter; push to main stays unfiltered. I changed the IMPL's allowlist to a denylist because the allowlist had real holes. Root unit tests import crawl-worker/lib and crawl-worker/sources (22 reachable files, including github-app-token.js and github-client.js) and read wrangler.jsonc, public/video, scanner-worker scripts, .specweave backups and mdx-components.tsx. The E2E workflow had no permissions block and relied on the repo default, unlike every other workflow here. It now declares contents: read. The E2E run passed with it, including the checkout of the public vskill repo.

review.pr_body:
Before: the unit-test check ran all 721 files in one job on a single worker, because Vitest defaults to cpus-1 workers on the 2-vCPU private runner. About 190 API-route tests ran in jsdom, every file loaded Testing Library, and one scanner test slept 18s through real retry backoffs. The job took about 14 minutes (main run 38926914511: 14m16s) and also ran on docs-only PRs. E2E fetched an unpinned wait-on package at run time and had no Next build cache.

After: the suite runs as four 2-worker shards on a cached node_modules, followed by a `vitest` check. That check fails unless every shard passed, merges the shard blob reports and enforces the 60% coverage thresholds over the same full-repo denominator (66.04%, 92018/139323, against 65.95% on main). Branch runs took 4m12s and 4m14s end to end. API-route tests run in node, Testing Library loads only where a DOM exists, the scanner test takes milliseconds, and a missing Prisma client fails fast and says how to fix it. The job summary lists per-shard totals and the slowest files, with warnings for files over 10s. PRs that touch only docs, or only crawl-worker files the root tests never import, skip the check. E2E waits with a bounded curl loop, restores the Next build cache (build 96s down to 65s) and runs with a read-only token.

How: `vitest-shard` is a 4-way matrix (`--shard=N/4 --maxWorkers=2`, blob and dot reporters, thresholds zeroed). Shard 1 keeps `coverage.all` on because `--merge-reports` never adds untested files; the other shards turn it off. The final `vitest` job runs with `if: !cancelled()`, fails on any shard result other than success, then runs `vitest run --merge-reports --coverage`. node_modules is cached per OS, arch, Node version, lockfile and .npmrc. `npm ci --ignore-scripts` runs only on a miss, and `npm run setup` always runs. Test setup yields one setImmediate turn after each test, so long synchronous files no longer hit Vitest's 60s "Timeout calling onTaskUpdate". A globalSetup check stops the run when the generated Prisma client is missing. The E2E Postgres service uses trust auth, so no connection string with credentials is committed.

Verification
- actionlint on both workflows: clean.
- unit tests run 38942617592: green in 4m14s; 719 files passed + 4 skipped, 7613 tests; Statements 66.04%.
- run 38941505624: one red shard made the `vitest` check fail at the gate in 5s.
- Re-running only failed jobs (38936816531 attempt 2) goes green; download-artifact takes the newest blob for each shard.
- 0826 E2E run 38941509144: green in 3m40s.
- Locally: all 194 src/app .test.ts files pass under node; an 18-file DOM sample passes; the scanner retry tests fail when the fake-timer advance is too short; a missing Prisma client exits 1 with the fix message; on a small set of files, merged shards reproduce the unsharded statement totals exactly, and the merge step fails below 60%.
- The NotificationsForm save test, which raced under two workers, now waits for Save to be enabled; the old version fails every time with a 20ms-slow load and the new one passes.

items.note: package.json now has deploy:build = db:generate && clean && build:worker && verify-queue-health-build, and deploy = deploy:build && wrangler deploy && verify-queue-health-deploy. That is one Next build, with Prisma generated first. A new script runs release = bash scripts/release.sh. push-deploy.sh no longer runs its own db:generate.

New scripts/release.sh (625 lines, bash 3.2, set -euo pipefail, BSD tools).
(a) Tree-equality CI gate: a successful unit-tests.yml run on the commit, or on a PR head with the same tree. A 422/404 from gh means no PR. --allow-untested overrides it.
(b) Migration diff against the live commit. It refuses without --migrate or --no-migrate, and also when the live commit is unknown. --deployed-sha supplies the commit.
(c) Runs npm ci && npm run setup only when the sha256 of package-lock.json plus the node version differs from node_modules/.release-lock-sha.
(d) Reads PREV from wrangler deployments status before building.
(e) Pins VSKILL_BUILD_DATA_DIR to the gitHead of the latest published vskill (--vskill-ref overrides). It is cached in .specweave/cache (gitignored), fetched from the sibling clone with git show or from codeload, and checked for agentPrefixes.
(f) One build (deploy:build) and one wrangler deploy, with --var RELEASE_GIT_SHA:<sha> so the next release knows which commit is live.
(g) Restores the four generated files.
(h) Reads the key with sed, no grep -P (scripts/lib/internal-key.sh); the key goes to curl through -H @-, never argv.
(i) --dry-run runs only read-only git/gh/wrangler/npm view queries. It exits 0 or 1 and lists every refusal. --sha builds an older main commit in a temporary worktree.
(j) Warns when a dependency bump ships with app changes and suggests a --sha split.
A lock dir stops two releases running at once, and a cleanup trap kills only PIDs the script started. scripts/release.test.mjs runs 8 sandbox tests against fake wrangler, gh and npm.

The CI gate inside release.sh accepts a passing run on a PR head with an identical tree, so a squash merge deploys without waiting for CI on main. A replay of incident commit 1f3fbaf6 is refused: the PR head tree differs and the main runs were cancelled. Branch protection is not changed (needs Anton).

release.sh warns when a release mixes a dependency change with app changes. It finds the first commit that changes dependencies (lockfile, or the dependency fields of package.json) and suggests --sha of the commit before it, or that commit alone. On the incident range it suggests releasing e621c981 first.

New scripts/verify-deploy-errors.mjs (456 lines, pure exported functions) with baseline, verify and analyze modes. It takes a 60s baseline on PREV during the build and a 90s tail filtered to the new version id. Exits: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error, 3 no traffic. release.sh rolls back to PREV and exits non-zero on any non-zero exit, on a smoke failure, or when a pass writes no report.
Threshold deviation (VERIFIER-backed): a flat 'at least 5 pg signatures' would roll back healthy deploys. Healthy production logs about 2 Connection terminated and about 2 TLS Handshake per minute. So each signature and failed invocations fail above max(4, 3x the baseline rate scaled to the window). 'This socket has been closed' has prior 1, so it fails at 5 or more even on a clean baseline (the incident had 638).
The real healthy recordings (tail6, tail7) pass. 18 node --test cases cover the fixtures healthy, pg-regression, noisy-baseline and empty, plus a fake-wrangler live tail and a symlinked-path regression (the first version silently exited 0 when started through /var).

push-deploy.sh sources scripts/lib/internal-key.sh. It reads the key with BSD sed from the environment, .dev.vars, .env.local or .env, in the same order as verify-queue-health-deploy.mjs, and sends it through stdin to curl. Its header now says it is an ungated legacy path.

README.md has a new Deploy section covering the command, gates, the error gate and rollback, the pinned build data, and that npm run deploy and push-deploy are ungated. The Development block line for deploy is corrected. AGENTS.md is new, with Setup (npm ci && npm run setup) and Deploy sections. Its rules include: never chain tests and a deploy with ;, no --allow-untested unless asked, and ship a dependency bump on its own release.
Covered by deploy:build running db:generate and by release.sh running npm run setup after any npm ci.

Only the reproducibility part is done: the build pins vskill data, and --sha builds an exact commit in a clean worktree. The CI-built artifact deploy was not done; the workflows belong to another agent and VERIFIER flagged artifact poisoning.

Before: a production deploy was a chain of manual steps. A separate build ran, then `npm run deploy` rebuilt everything, sometimes without a Prisma client. issues.summary: The automatic rollback could hang on a terminal. review.pr_body:
Before: a production deploy was a chain of manual steps. A separate build ran, then `npm run deploy` rebuilt everything, sometimes without a Prisma client. Nothing checked CI, so an untested squash merge or a mixed dependency bump could ship. The build read agents.json from whatever ../vskill branch was checked out locally, and the cache-warm key lookup used grep -P, which never matched on macOS. Regressions were caught by watching wrangler tail by hand. During the pg 8.23 incident the broken Worker served production for about 12 minutes before a manual rollback.

After: `npm run release` is one gated command. It refuses an untested tree, undecided migrations, a missing smoke key or a missing rollback target, and it installs only when the lockfile changed. It builds once with pinned vskill data, checks that the rollback target is still live, and records the deployed commit on the Worker. It compares a 60s pre-deploy error baseline with a 90s post-deploy tail plus the queue-health smoke, and rolls back to the previous version on its own, with no prompt, when a pg-socket regression appears, the smoke fails, the tail cannot watch the full window, or wrangler deploy fails after going live.

How: `scripts/release.sh` (bash 3.2, BSD tools) runs the CI gate. It accepts a successful unit-tests.yml run on the commit, or on a PR head with an identical git tree, so a squash merge of an up-to-date green PR deploys without waiting for main CI. It then checks migrations against the commit recorded in the live version's RELEASE_GIT_SHA, warns about dependency/app mixes with a `--sha` split suggestion, pins `VSKILL_BUILD_DATA_DIR` to the published vskill gitHead, runs `npm run deploy:build` (db:generate, clean, one OpenNext build, contract checks) and `wrangler deploy --var RELEASE_GIT_SHA:<sha>`, and restores the generated files. `scripts/verify-deploy-errors.mjs` keeps its parsing and decision logic in exported functions. Each signature is compared with its own baseline rate, because healthy production logs about two Connection terminated and two TLS Handshake errors a minute. "This socket has been closed" fails at 5 even on a clean baseline. `--dry-run` runs only read-only queries and lists every refusal. `scripts/push-deploy.sh` now pushes and then runs the release. `npm run deploy` stays as the ungated path and now generates the Prisma client first.

review.pr_title: release: faster desktop pipeline with nightly caches and release script
review.pr_body:
Before: Every desktop release waited about 6 minutes on a version-bump PR before the tag could go out. The tag build then compiled every Rust dependency cold on all three legs, because nothing on main wrote a Rust cache that tag builds could read. The Linux leg spent about 5 minutes building the RPM one step after another. The DMG users download was never notarized, the signing secrets were re-uploaded on every run, and release-desktop.sh was so stale that releases were done by hand. Nightly failures stayed red for weeks without anyone being told.

After: release-desktop.sh tags main's head directly, after a preflight with no side effects. It then watches the run and checks the release assets, the R2 manifest and the shipped bundle's updater signature. CI stamps the version from the tag and refuses a tag that is not on main. A Desktop Build nightly builds all three platforms from main and is the only writer of the pinned Rust caches that tag builds read. RPM builds on its own parallel leg and R2 uploads run in parallel. The DMG is notarized and stapled, and checks that fail the job verify it. latest.json can no longer be downgraded by accident. Pull requests and dispatches get a build-only dry run. A warn-only timing report flags slow steps and cache misses, and nightly-health keeps one issue open per red nightly on main.

The desktop release becomes one command whose wall time is CI time, and regressions in that time or in the nightly signals now show up on their own.

How: desktop-release.yml pins Rust 1.99.1 and the third-party actions by SHA. It restores rust-cache with `shared-key: desktop-<target>` and `save-if: false`, and restores the npm cache read-only. It splits RPM into a fourth matrix leg and runs tauri-action build-only. softprops uploads every asset once, after the R2 publish. Each leg signs a probe file with the updater key before compiling. The DMG goes through notarize-macos.sh with the same Apple ID credential the app uses, so the notarytool store-credentials step and the Homebrew step are gone. The workflow is least-privilege, with contents: write on publish only. Publish has its own concurrency group, and a lockfile stamp failure is now an error. notarize-dryrun.yml (renamed Desktop Build (nightly)) adds Linux and Windows legs and runs on schedule, on dispatch, and on pushes to main that touch src-tauri/**. Push runs skip macOS, so a green push run never counts as a passing notarization in nightly-health or in the release preflight. publish-manifest.sh uploads in parallel, deduped, and refuses to replace a newer live latest.json unless FORCE_ROLLBACK=1. src-tauri builds the lib as rlib only. RELEASING.md documents the npm and desktop commands, dry runs, guards and failure recovery.

Verification:
- actionlint and yaml.safe_load are clean on all three workflows; bash -n passes on every script with /bin/bash 3.2.
- `release-desktop.sh --dry-run` against the live repo: rc 0, picks 1.0.66, verifies the live 1.0.65 macOS bundle signature. A snapshot diff of tags, releases and secrets shows no change.
- release-desktop.sh with a stubbed gh/git: a red canary, including a red scheduled notarization hidden behind a green push run, stops a real run before anything is pushed.
- publish-manifest.sh against a stub aws: parallel deduped uploads; downgrade refused; failed upload leaves latest.json untouched; FORCE_ROLLBACK and DRY_RUN behave as documented.
- The signing probe, run with a throwaway key, passes with the right passphrase and fails on a wrong passphrase or a mismatched pubkey.
- nightly-health script body against a stub gh: create, comment, close, partial-run no-close, stale-run and cancelled-run cases.
- The new macOS gate commands pass on the live 1.0.65 .app and reject the live, unnotarized 1.0.65 DMG.
- `cargo update -p vskill-desktop --precise` moves only that lock entry when Cargo.toml is ahead of the lock. `cargo check --locked` passes with crate-type rlib.
- timing-report.mjs self-test passes, and a live report on the 1.0.65 run flags the cold caches and the RPM step. Report failures become warnings and exit 0.

impl.before_after:
Before: every PR waited on one runner running the whole Vitest suite, about 3.5 minutes. Any push to a fix/** branch started a full 9-minute Windows Rust job, even when no Rust code had changed. That job ran cargo check, then cargo test --no-run, then cargo test, all on a cold cache, after building the real frontend and sidecar only to satisfy tauri-build. Two Windows settings tests failed now and then because they slept a fixed 350 ms and hoped the background write had landed. The npm release ran the full suite again, built everything twice, and only found out about a dead npm token at the publish step. Tagging and checking the release was all done by hand.

After: the full suite runs in three parallel shards, and a single unit-full check still reports their combined result. Superseded PR runs are cancelled and every job has a timeout. The Windows Rust job runs one cargo test against stub prerequisites, with a pinned toolchain and one cache that main writes and PRs read. The settings tests wait for the exact write they asked for. The npm release checks npm credentials in seconds, restores main's npm cache without saving its own, waits for CI on the tagged commit instead of re-running tests, and builds once. tsx is now pinned. scripts/release/release-npm.sh tags origin/main, follows the run and confirms the package on the registry and through npx, and --dry-run checks everything without tagging.

issues.summary: The restore-only npm cache missed on almost every release. The version bump changes package-lock.json, and main's CI for that commit saves its cache only after the tag run has already tried to restore. Added a restore-keys prefix (node-cache-<os>-<arch>-npm-) so the run falls back to main's newest npm cache. I confirmed main has caches under that prefix.

The job timeout stayed at 20 minutes, but the job now waits on the whole ci.yml run, which includes macOS and Windows jobs that can queue and have 15-minute timeouts each. Raised it to 30 minutes and added a comment.
The credentials probe said the user was 'not an owner of vskill' even when `npm owner ls` itself had failed. Separated the two failures. The owner list, which includes emails, is never printed.

--dry-run never checked HTTPS git push credentials, so missing credentials only showed up at the real tag push. Added `git push --dry-run` of the tag to the preflight. It sends no objects and no ref update. Tested both ways against a scratch bare remote: it passes normally and fails when the push URL points at a missing repo. No tag was created anywhere.

Two commit subjects were 73 and 74 characters, over the 72-character limit. Rebuilt the branch with shortened subjects. The tree is identical to the pre-rewrite head (git diff --quiet 84214e2 vs new head). Pushed with --force-with-lease against the old remote SHA dc4ca96.

Before: Every PR waited on one runner running the whole Vitest suite, about 3.5 minutes. Any push to a fix/** branch started a full 9-minute Windows Rust job, even when no Rust code had changed. That job ran cargo check, then cargo test --no-run, then cargo test, all on a cold cache, after building the real frontend and sidecar only to satisfy tauri-build. Two Windows settings tests failed now and then because they slept a fixed 350 ms and hoped the background write had landed. The npm release re-ran the full suite on a commit CI was already testing, built everything twice, and only found out about a dead npm token at the publish step. Tagging and checking a release was done by hand.

After: The full suite runs in three parallel shards, and a single unit-full check still reports their combined result. Superseded PR runs are cancelled and every job has a timeout. The Windows Rust job runs one cargo test against stub prerequisites, with a pinned toolchain and one cache that main writes and PRs read. It now takes about 4 minutes cold, against 8.5 before. The settings tests wait for the exact write they asked for. The npm release checks npm credentials in seconds and restores main's npm cache without saving its own, falling back to main's newest cache when the bump changed the lockfile. It waits for CI on the tagged commit instead of re-running tests, and it builds once. tsx is pinned. scripts/release/release-npm.sh tags origin/main, follows the release run, and confirms the package on the registry and through npx. Its --dry-run checks everything, push credentials included, without tagging.

How: ci.yml turns unit-full into a 3-way `vitest --shard` matrix. An aggregate `unit-full` job (needs + !cancelled()) fails unless every shard passed. ci.yml and sidecar-smoke.yml get concurrency groups keyed on the PR number or the SHA, and only PR runs are cancelled. sidecar-smoke.yml drops the unfiltered fix/** push and adds push to main with the same paths. rust-windows stubs dist/eval-ui/index.html and the sidecar exe, pins dtolnay 1.99.1 and uses rust-cache v2.9.2 with shared-key rust-windows-debug and save-if on main. The sidecar build is pinned to Node 22.23.3. In settings.rs, set_key hands out a request generation under the state lock. The debouncer drains generations under the same lock, writes, then publishes the highest generation it wrote on a watch channel. flush_for_test waits, with a 10s limit, until the written generation reaches the requested one. npm-release.yml probes `npm whoami` and package ownership first, restores the npm cache with actions/cache/restore and never saves it, and watches the ci.yml push run for the tag SHA, falling back to `npm test` if there is none. It then publishes through prepublishOnly, which builds and runs the preflight. tsx 4.23.15 is now an exact devDependency.

issues.summary: All develop pushes shared one concurrency group with cancel-in-progress. A bump-only or docs-only push therefore cancelled the previous code commit's test run, then skipped its own tests, so that code was never tested and release.yml's gate would refuse the release (98a8ce00d was cancelled this way today). Each push to develop or main now gets its own group (test-<ref>-<sha>); PRs still cancel superseded runs.

'Publish GitHub Release' read isDraft inside [ "$(gh release view ...)" != true ]. A failed lookup did not trip set -e, so the step printed 'already published', exited 0 and left the release as a draft. The value is now assigned first, so a failed lookup fails the step.

The CI gate checked $GITHUB_SHA. On a manual run that bumps the version, the released commit is the local bump commit, so a minor or major release passed on tests of the pre-bump code. The gate now checks HEAD: a patch bump falls back to the tested parent, and a minor or major bump is refused. That bump-and-push path is already blocked by branch protection.

The new npm ci ran after the global npm 12.0.2 upgrade, a combination no other job uses and nobody tested. It now runs with Node 22's own npm, like every Test & Validate job, and npm 12 is installed afterwards for the OIDC publish.

No test covered the safety-critical event binding (pull_request: HEAD^2 must equal the PR head; push: HEAD^1 must equal event.before; any other event runs the tests). issues.summary: Stopping a gate left its work running. run-tests.sh, pr-gate.sh and typecheck-gate.sh start each job in its own process group, and background jobs in a non-interactive shell ignore INT, so Ctrl-C or a parent's TERM killed only the wrapper. Every python test, tsc and vitest suite kept running as an orphan. This was reproduced. It also meant verify-release's step timeout could not stop the fleet step, because the orphans held its output pipes open. Fixed: a shared jobs.sh (job_run, job_pool) runs the xargs pool in its own group and traps INT, TERM and HUP. Each job gets TERM, then KILL after 5s. A TERM to a PR gate running nested pools (typecheck, fleet, packages) now leaves no process and exits 143 within 4s.

Killing a shard on timeout or a signal sent SIGTERM to its vp process only. The vitest workers kept running tests into the TMPDIR being removed, rmSync threw ENOTEMPTY, and the runner crashed with exit 1 before writing shards.json. This was reproduced: the orphans were still running 40s later. Fixed: each shard is a detached process-group leader, timeouts and signals go to the whole group, leftovers are KILLed when a shard closes, and cleanup uses retries without crashing. After TERM the runner now exits 143 with both TMPDIRs removed and no workers left.

`pnpm run test:fleet -- --out DIR`, the documented form, failed with 'unknown option: --' because pnpm 11 passes the `--` through. The same happened for verify:pr and typecheck:gate. test:server:sharded treated it as the start of the vitest filters, so `--out` went missing. Fixed in all four scripts, with a parseArgs test.
A typecheck that crashed (abort or signal exit) after printing only baselined diagnostics counted as explained and passed. Only tsc's diagnostic exits 1 and 2 are now explained. Added a test case.
When a timed-out job's leader exited on TERM, the watchdog was cancelled before its KILL, so grandchildren that ignore TERM survived. This was reproduced. The group is now KILLed after any timeout.

A non-numeric FLEET_TEST_TIMEOUT, PR_GATE_TIMEOUT or TYPECHECK_TIMEOUT made the watchdog's sleep fail at once, so every job was reported as an instant TIMEOUT. The value is now validated, and the script exits 2 with a clear message.

The pooled fleet suite and the all-package typecheck gate each ran under the single 600s default step cap. That cap used to apply to each of 7 separate suites and 3 typechecks. At load ~600 the fleet run took 811s. Both steps now get 1200s, and each runner still bounds its own jobs.

The SIGBUS demonstration test slept a fixed 0.3s before polling the holder, so it failed whenever a loaded host had not yet scheduled the holder. It now waits up to 30s for the holder to exit. The negative check keeps its 0.3s, and the SIGBUS assertion is unchanged.
The background-priority probe's 60s subprocess timeout flaked under load (it hit in the implementer's run and in mine). It is now 300s; the assertions are unchanged.

Under load ~600 the SIGBUS test can still end with the holder exiting 1 on 'database is locked' (SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY) instead of SIGBUS, which is a race in the test's design. I left the assertion alone so the test is not weakened.
On a saturated host (load ~600), the Darwin background band gets no CPU, so the probe still times out even at 300s. No timeout can fix this.

The gate cannot pass on main. The scripts package's node:test half has 10 failures that predate this branch: 7 confirmed locally (release-version, runtime-package, preservation-audit) and 3 in shared-fleet-workflow per the implementer. None of those files are touched here.

impl.before_after:
Before: A SpecWithCode release was put together by hand from shell history. The environment came from several places, the full server suite ran twice, and web and contrast failures showed up only after the 22-minute server run, which forced a second signed build. The server bundle and Google check ran after signing, fleet tools lived outside the repo, the public release went out before any fleet host was updated, and nothing recorded how long each step took.

After: `bash scripts/release/release.sh <version>` runs the whole release as resumable stages:
- It checks the environment from a paths-only release.env and reuses persistent trees.
- It runs the fast suites in parallel before the signed build, with the server suite once alongside the build and only on changed files after a fix.
- It verifies the bundle and Google sign-in before signing, and drafts both releases while the suites run.
- It then publishes private, updates M4, then M1 and M3, on installed version, then publishes public and swaps the desktop app.

It prints each stage's time next to the previous release's. `--dry-run` shows every command, and `--self-test` checks the script with stubbed commands.

issues.summary: stage_plan left out update.py's --allow-project-migrations by default (MIGRATIONS=0). Every plan from 1.0.30 to 1.0.37 passed it, so any release containing a project migration would have failed and rolled back on every host. It is now on by default, and --no-project-migrations turns it off.

When the lookup of the previous release failed, init_state had already created the staging folder but no release.json. Every later run then refused that folder as not made by release.sh, so the release was stuck until someone deleted it by hand. The lookup now runs before the folder exists, and a failed gh/python pipeline gives a clear error instead of a silent set -e exit.

stage_server_wait could loop forever: it ran `continue` whenever server.exit existed, even when that result belonged to an old candidate and the server was dead. A new server_result helper fixes this, and the stage now fails with --resume guidance when the suite stops without a result.

When a host's guarded install failed (the update rolled back), the rollout kept polling until its deadline, and each new request restarted the service only to fail the same way. update_request status now reports lastInstall. fleet_rollout stops when a failed install of this version is dated at or after its first request on the host's own clock, unless the install timed out and was left to finish.

The bump stage's `git checkout -B release/<v> FETCH_HEAD` silently reset a local release branch that held unpushed commits. It now refuses when that branch has any commit other than its own 'Prepare SpecWithCode <v> release'.

A new candidate's stage runs `git clean -fdx` in the build tree, so a new fix file left out of the commit was deleted. A new candidate with untracked, non-ignored files is now refused before the push and the clean, and the refusal lists the first 5 files.

If publish.mjs tagged and then its push failed, the tag was left only in the public clone. On --resume, `publish.mjs --tag` refused that existing tag, after the private release and the fleet rollout were already done. When the remote has no tag, publish-public now deletes the local one first.

The drafts stage uploaded every asset even when the background server suite had already failed, and server-wait then deleted them. Drafts now stops before any upload and deletes an earlier candidate's drafts.
load_google_pair dropped the last line of the Google pair file when it had no trailing newline. That left out a client variable, and the bundle stage's Google check then failed.
`--status` is described as changing no release state, but it rewrites the derived timings/stages.json. That is harmless, so it is left as is.

Spec item F7, rerunning only the server suite's failed files, is not implemented; after a fix it uses vitest --changed instead. The per-package vitest JSON timings in the spec are also not added. Both are follow-ups.
Whether verify-bundle.mjs accepts an archive is detected by grepping it for 'tar\.gz'. That works with perf/release-gates, but it is a heuristic.

review.pr_body:
Before: a release was a long sequence of steps run by hand from a staging script outside the repo: bump, tests, build, sign, helpers, plan, drafts, publish to two repositories, roll out to M4 and then M1 and M3, and swap the desktop app. After a failure, someone had to work out which steps to repeat. The fleet was watched for "downloaded" rather than installed. The helpers builder and the guarded manual update were not in the repo.

After: `bash scripts/release/release.sh <version>` runs every stage in order. Each stage gets a marker, a log and a timing, and the run stops at the first failure with the command to continue. `--resume` skips the stages already done. A fix commit becomes the new candidate and reruns only the per-candidate stages: stage 1 runs last time's failures first, and the server suite runs with `--changed`. `--stop-after drafts` prepares everything without publishing, and `--dry-run` prints every command and writes nothing. The rollout waits for each host's installed version, M4 first, and stops when a host's guarded install fails.

How: release.sh is bash 3.2. It keeps its state in `~/.specwithcode/release-staging/<version>/`, runs the server suite in the background in its own process group, and compares stage timings with the previous release. `release_tools.py` handles sums, notes, the public notes filter, the Google pair and timings. `update_request.py` gains request and status commands, and status now also reports `lastInstall`. `fleet_rollout.py` handles the M4-first order. `make_helpers.py` and `remote_update.py` are ported into the repo, and `make_update_plan.py --previous-plan` takes its upgrade sources from the previous release. Plans pass `--allow-project-migrations` and `--allow-existing-browser-heartbeat` by default, as 1.0.30 to 1.0.37 did; `--no-project-migrations` leaves out the first. The run refuses or stops on several unsafe states:
- a local `release/<version>` with unpushed work;
- untracked files the candidate clean would delete;
- a server suite that already failed, before any draft upload;
- a server suite that stopped without a result.

It also keeps working through these:
- it recovers from a failed lookup of the previous release without leaving a stuck staging folder;
- it drops a stale local public tag on resume;
- it keeps a Google pair whose last line has no newline.

It depends on perf/release-gates for `test-sharded.mjs`, `typecheck-gate.sh`, `run-tests.sh` and the archive-aware `verify-bundle.mjs`, so merge that branch first.

Verification
- `bash scripts/release/release.sh --self-test` under /bin/bash 3.2: 28 passed, 0 failed. Each new guard was mutation-checked: removing it makes its test fail.
- `python3 -B scripts/studio-fleet/test-fleet-rollout.py`: 19 tests OK on python3 and /usr/bin/python3.
- `bash -n` on both scripts. There are no bash 4 or GNU-only constructs.
- `--dry-run` lists every stage in order and writes nothing under HOME.
- `git merge-tree` merges clean with main and with perf/release-gates. The interfaces match that branch's scripts.

impl.before_after:
Before: Each repo was released by hand, from memory notes that had gone stale: a triple platform build, a manual OTP npm publish, and a desktop note holding the literal signing passphrase. Waits were ad hoc, often blocking past the tool cap. Nobody tracked step timings or linted the workflows, and MEMORY.md was 27.8KB, so its tail, including the Studio release pointers, never loaded.

After: One umbrella entrypoint, scripts/release/release.sh, audits all four repos in about 7s and verifies every track deterministically. It ships a track as script, then verify, then gated cleanup, all driven by a public-safe manifest. ci-wait.sh caps waits at 540s with exit codes 0/1/2 and ETag polling, and timing.py records step timings and flags regressions. Its CI lint found 123 issues. Memory is 17.5KB with release pointers at the top, notes describe the current commands, and no passphrase remains in memory.

issues.summary: ship --dry-run passed --dry-run to track scripts without checking they support it; the current shared vskill release-desktop.sh has no such flag and would take it as VERSION, then run gh secret set, bump, commit and tag. ship_track now reads the dry-run flag from the manifest and refuses (plan: 'would refuse'; run: die) when the script lacks it.

cleanup counted unique commits with `git cherry | grep -c` under pipefail. A cherry error or SIGPIPE, or a missing origin/<default>, read as 0 unique commits, so unmerged worktrees were marked merged and their branches force-deleted. Now unique_commits returns non-zero on git failure, cleanup dies without refs/remotes/origin/<default>, and every git error keeps the worktree.

cleanup had no guard for worktrees in active use (AC requires keeping in-flight work). Added an idle guard from the mtimes of HEAD, index and logs/HEAD; manifest cleanup.min_idle_minutes defaults to 30.

pr mode returned PASS once the current check-runs were green, before `needs:` jobs or queued workflows had created check runs, and NONE exited 0 too early. It now also queries actions/runs?head_sha=, waits on incomplete non-noise runs, and NONE needs the head to be older than 300s and at least 60s elapsed.

Tracks shipping in parallel shared fixed temp paths (gate JSON, cleanup JSONL, worktree error file, HTTP body and header files), so one track could read another's cleanup gate. All are now per-track or mktemp files under $WORK.

ship exited 0 while verify was still pending, and a cleanup die failed a track that had already shipped. Pending now exits 2 and later tracks continue; cleanup runs in a subshell and its problems are recorded in the result text.
verify --version silently applied one version to every track in a group. It now dies when the group has more than one track.
state_set read-modify-write raced across parallel tracks; it now holds an fcntl lock.

Several fixes: timing appends now take a lock; a cache miss counts once per run instead of once per log line; a change of action version no longer looks like a cache-key change; invalid YAML has its own workflow-invalid rule; worktrees match the manifest by origin slug; the vitest rule no longer flags --merge-reports or echo and comment lines; history check_name is URL-encoded.

The ETag cache could pair a stale body with a new ETag, and its files were written non-atomically. Bodies are now keyed by ETag checksum and written with mktemp plus mv; entries older than 24h are pruned; usage no longer prints code lines.

review.pr_title: 0925: umbrella release entrypoint, CI-wait helper and timing scanner
review.pr_body:
Before: each repo was released with its own script and a hand-run checklist. Waiting on CI meant polling in the foreground or sleeping. Nobody tracked how long release steps took, so slow steps and cache misses went unnoticed, and merged worktrees piled up.

After: `scripts/release/release.sh` runs status, ship, verify and cleanup for every track in `.specweave/release/manifest.json`. `ci-wait.sh` waits on a run, PR, URL, log or npm version with a bounded budget and ETag polling. `timing.py` records step timings, flags regressions and cache misses, and lints CI workflows.

How: the manifest holds repos, tracks, groups, policy, known-noise checks and protected paths. ship runs each repo's own release script in parallel per repo, then verify and cleanup. It refuses a dry run when the track script has no dry-run option, and exits 2 while verify is still pending. Cleanup removes a worktree only when it has no unique commits against origin's default branch (or its PR merged at the exact tip), it is idle for at least 30 minutes, and every git call succeeded. PR mode in ci-wait also waits on workflow runs that have not created check runs yet. Shared state and timing writes are locked, and temp files are per track.

Verification
- bash -n on all scripts under bash 3.2.57; `timing.py --self-test`: 17 tests OK
- `release.sh status`, `verify platform` and `ship all --plan` against the live repos
- Fixtures for cleanup: missing origin ref, unmerged and recently active worktrees kept, only the merged idle worktree removed
- Fixtures for ship: dry-run refusal, exit 2 on pending, cleanup failure isolated
- ci-wait against real runs, PRs, latest.json, logs and npm, plus jq verdict fixtures
- `scan-ci` and `timing.py check` against the shared checkouts
